title: Kilagen Framework Clause Vocabulary
description: Validates one framework edition: its clause list, and optionally the structure the framework itself publishes. Resolved from keel/content/frameworks/<id>.yml (shipped with the package) or, when an instance overrides or adds one, program/model/frameworks/<id>.yml. The file stem is the framework id and must match a config.yml frameworks[].id.
$comment: REFERENCE-NOT-COPY, AND WHERE THE LINE IS. A clause may carry its official `name`, because a name is an identifier — 'PR.AA Identity Management' says something, 'PR.AA' says nothing. A `description` must be written in our own words, brief and generic; if it reads like the standard's prose, it is a copy and it is wrong. The normative text is never reproduced here: it lives behind `resources`, at the publisher's own URL. Do not 'complete' these descriptions from the standard.

name.description: The edition's human name, e.g. 'NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0'.

description.description: What this framework is and who it applies to, in our own words. Never copied from the standard.

granularity.description: The level the clause list is pinned at, e.g. 'CSF 2.0 Categories (22)'. The denominator is half of any coverage percentage, so it has to be visible.

resources.description: Where to read the normative text. This is what makes reference-not-copy work: whoever needs the wording goes to the publisher.

groups.description: The structure the framework publishes — functions, requirement families, themes, criteria. Optional: a framework that publishes a flat list gets a flat list, and nothing invents structure for it.

clauses.description: Flat clause list, for a framework with no published grouping. Mutually exclusive with 'groups'.

clause.description: A clause reference: the bare ref, or the ref with its official name and our own short description.

oneOf.description: Quote every value so a numeric-looking ref (e.g. "13.60") is not collapsed to a float by the YAML parser.

id.description: The publisher's own identifier for the group, e.g. 'GV' or 'A.5'.

color.description: The framework's own colour for this group, where it publishes one. Identity, never a score: nothing in this file may encode how well a clause is met.

center.description: This group sits at the centre of the wheel rather than on the rim — NIST CSF's Govern function, which the framework itself draws that way.
